graph.title: Zero-temperature SK full support, scalar value, and the separate QAOA manuscript target
graph.scope: Manually curated, source-grounded intake of two public formal interfaces and a distinct broader manuscript claim. The default selection is the full-support interface. The graph has no extracted Lean dependency edges and supplies no checked proof, semantic certification, or reader acceptance.
notes: All content is anchored to public OpenAI sources at adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a; mathlib metadata and licence retain their separate pinned revision. Local source paths are relative to this graph file directory.

This is a manually curated intake. Its formalizes edges record mappings named by the public scope and Comparator configs; they are not Lean dependency extraction or an independent proof of statement equivalence.

The 347 vendored OAI modules form two static import closures. Their internal declarations and proof terms have not been exported into this graph; an absent dependency edge must not be read as dependency independence.

The QAOA introduction (lines 50–72) names a primary zero-temperature companion route and an independent positive-temperature route. No cross-manuscript supports edges are asserted because correspondence between those imported scalar formulations and these exact formal interfaces has not been independently reviewed.

The whole QAOA theorem remains a separate unverified manuscript target. Selecting or explaining full_support or scalar_value must not be reported as formal verification of QAOA circuit-energy convergence.

The original intake recorded planned, unrun checks. A separately retained standalone full-support Comparator attempt was unavailable before startup; it was not a mathematical rejection. No completed research replay, axiom audit or elaborated research dependency extraction is established by these records. Fixture and Minimal-tool checks do not supply research-target evidence. Independent complete manuscript review and human reader review remain open.
The three axioms named in the Comparator configs are the permitted-axiom policy, not the output of an axiom audit. Both configs set enable_nanoda=false.

The challenge statements intentionally contain sorry; the implementing proof sources are separate. Source acquisition and hashing do not establish that those implementations compile or satisfy the challenge under the permitted axioms.

The original full OpenAI package has unrelated dependencies and patch hooks; the active minimal package and all derivation inputs are identified in source-lock.json. The two exact manuscript trees and PDFs are vendored under the repository root Apache-2.0 licence, with original READMEs; the secondary Latent Seminar article is reference-only.

R2-25 semantic extension: every supports edge runs from a consumer statement to an ingredient used in the selected cited proof. Multiple outgoing edges do not individually entail the consumer and do not claim a logically minimal premise set. Case guards stay in statements and warrants: support.no_bounded_gap invokes support.positive_curvature when c>0 and support.zero_curvature when c=0, not both guards simultaneously. This is a proof by cases within one selected route, not a union of alternative proof attempts. All support.* records remain unverified.

R2-25 quantifiers: analytic nodes universally quantify admissible gamma, and smooth-step nodes separately quantify finite-step data and their smooth terminal value. Minimizer-dependent claims retain assumptions.full_support_minimizer. A hypothetical positive, zero, initial or terminal plateau is a local conditional guard, never an unconditional additional assumption of full_support. All uses of q in one inference refer to the same coefficient, value function, Brownian system and associated diffusion.

R2-25 relation boundaries: formalizes is curated statement correspondence; supports is authored mathematical use; node.citation_ids and citations.source_id own references; source_id/revision/sha256 own provenance. Lean source links here are citations/navigation, not lean_type_dependency or lean_value_dependency edges. Paper reading order and passage correspondence stay in the existing paper mappings and are not logical proof premises.

R2-25 source-level leaves: support.regularity, support.stieltjes_measure, support.step_tails and support.rational_certificate deliberately package cited proofs or standard constructions. The graph does not enumerate their heat-kernel, probability, measure-theory, algebra or proof-assistant transitive dependencies. A zero outgoing-edge count is therefore not a completeness claim.

R2-25 boundaries outside the selection: minimizer existence, the Parisi ground-state formula, smooth density, scalar formal-model transport and QAOA synthesis/transfer are not inferred from this support subgraph. Pedagogical two-spin, zero-candidate and missing-area examples are illustrations and have no supports edges into the theorem.

R2-25 application scope: support.strict_increase states the general implication from full relative support to strict increase and its selected minimizer application. Its supports edge to support.full_relative_support records how that application supplies the antecedent. The dependency closure is for this chosen application; it does not assert that the generic measure-theoretic implication requires minimization.

R2-25 historical evidence: every pre-existing receipt and its scope is preserved. Those receipts describe the captured intake observations and are not an exhaustive chronology of external runs; no source-unbound later observation is promoted to a public successful build or comparison.
